Today, it’s a powerful sales tool - one that can inspire customers, streamline the buying journey, and capture valuable data along the way.

item.title: Turn a Static PDF into a High-Performing Digital Brochure
item.description: Most organisations still rely on PDFs when producing brochures - they’re familiar, easy to lay out, and simple to export from design tools. But in a world where audiences expect mobile-friendly design, intuitive navigation, interactive content, and trackable behaviour, a PDF on its own no longer meets the mark.

item.title: Digital Publishing Trends for 2026: What's Next
item.description: As 2025 draws to a close, the digital publishing landscape feels more confident and more forward-looking than it has in years. Publishers have spent this year refining their digital strategies, strengthening accessibility, and rethinking how their content connects with wider ecosystems.

item.title: Predicting the Digital Publishing Trends for 2026
item.description: After a busy 2025 - a year shaped by the European Accessibility Act, the rise of mobile-first reading habits, and huge leaps in AI-powered production - digital publishing heads into 2026 with even more momentum. Audiences are expecting richer experiences, regulators are paying closer attention, and digital platforms are evolving fast to keep up.

item.title: 2025 Year in Review: How Digital Publishing Evolved
item.description: As 2025 draws to a close, it’s clear that this has been a formative year for digital publishing. Not necessarily a year defined by bold, flashy breakthroughs, but one marked by meaningful shifts: accessibility turning into obligation, AI becoming more practical and reader-facing, and digital publications taking a more strategic role inside broader digital ecosystems.

item.title: The Digital Publisher Checklist: How to Kick Off 2026 the Right Way
item.description: As we enter the first full working of 2026, we begin to ponder on the challenges of digital publishing for the year to come. Reader expectations will be higher, privacy regulations are tighter, accessibility is no longer optional, and competition for attention will be fiercer than ever. For publishers using a digital publishing platform, the start of the year is the perfect moment to step back, review what you have in place, and make sure your setup is working as hard as it should be.

item.title: What to Expect from UK Digital Accessibility Requirements in 2026
item.description: As we move through 2026, digital accessibility is becoming a more prominent consideration for organisations publishing and maintaining digital content in the UK. While the legal framework itself has not radically changed, expectations around compliance, enforcement, and best practice are continuing to evolve.
